readThisBeforeReusingTheseRows: groundTruth is `by-construction`, not `human-review`, and the difference is load-bearing. A corpus label says 'somebody read this third-party code and judged it'; these rows say 'this code was WRITTEN to be an instance, and here are the lines'. That is why humanConfirmed is true here while it is false on every row of the real label set, and why no rate is withheld here: there is no judgement to be unreviewed. These rows measure the SCORER. They say nothing about any tool's accuracy on real code.
